source.author: hor
source.text: amphora coepit institui: currente rota cur urceus exit?
source.text_original: amphora coepit  / institui: currente rota cur urceus exit?
source.text_english: An amphora has begun to be made; why, while the wheel is running, does a pitcher come out?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Verum, ne Flaccus de nobis rideat amphora coepit institui: currente rota cur urceus exit? , reuertimur ad nostros bipedes asellos et in eorum aurem bucina magis quam cithara concrepamus.
reuse.text_original: Verum, ne Flaccus de nobis rideat — amphora coepit institui: currente rota cur urceus exit?— , reuertimur ad nostros bipedes asellos et in eorum aurem bucina magis quam cithara concrepamus.
reuse.text_english: But lest Flaccus laugh at us, the jar has begun to be shaped: when the wheel is running, why does the pitcher come out? We return to our own two-footed little donkeys and sound the trumpet rather than the lyre in their ear.
